original_card.question: Can a specified pair of consecutive calls eliminate a restoration that the next call reconstructs?
methods: Write typed entry/exit contracts and a contracting multitype recurrence.
Derive a lower bound for the compulsory transitions of one proposed typed interface.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show actual eliminated work and legal composition; changing a scalar recurrence into a matrix is insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Find a concrete consecutive-call boundary in the selected review and list its entry/exit obligations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Specify two call types and one operation actually removed by composition; derive the normalized recurrence.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Eliminating compulsory boundary work can lower recursive cost beyond packing gains.
allowed_variations: A two-type pilot or one explicit deferred restoration.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting the old scalar recurrence as a matrix without eliminating work.

actual_scope: Exact minimum paid scalar XOR adapters for 4808 fixed two-output/two-workspace binary call chains of lengths 1..3, with partial output observations and arbitrary dirty inputs.
scope_change_reason: A finite abstract replacement interface is studied instead of asserting a selected-supplier call pair. Intermediate observations may leave workspace and unobserved output rows noncanonical; the earlier fully restored diagonal partition model excludes this state space.
bottleneck_link: Scoped interface side result: exact adapter tariffs show when partial observations eliminate boundary work. No selected recursive profile or kappa improvement follows without a real caller and fully charged physical binding.
stop_rule: Exhaust exactly lengths 1..3 and the declared six-adapter/eight-child alphabet; do not expand the domain or infer native admission. Reserve final quarter of a 60-minute session for checks and handoff.
evidence: RESULT.json: two independent exact searches agree on 4808 instances; 100 partial-observation improvements, none of the 1824 instances with both update rows nonzero; 76928 literal dirty-input runs and 10 failure controls. README supplies the finite-state completeness proof and direct sharp 1-versus-3 proof.

ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in scoping, mathematics, implementation, verification and writing; no independent human or proof-assistant review.
